pr.title: Fix Box allocator drop elaboration
pr.description:
New version of rust-lang/rust#131146.

Clearing Box's drop flag after running its destructor can cause it to skip dropping its allocator, so just don't. Its cleared by the drop ladder code afterwards already.

Unlike the last PR this also handles other types with destructors properly, in the event that we can have open drops on them in the future (by partial initialization or DerefMove or something).

Finally, I also added tests for the interaction with async drop here but I discovered rust-lang/rust#143658, so one of the tests has a `knownbug` annotation. Not sure if it should be in this PR at all though.

Fixes rust-lang/rust#131082

pr.author: beepster4096

issues.title: Box sometimes forgets to drop its allocator when the Box is conditionally initialized.

analysis.originalLogic: In `ElaborateDrops`, `open_drop_for_adt` builds an open-drop ladder for an ADT: for a union or `ManuallyDrop` it skips contents, otherwise it calls `open_drop_for_adt_contents`; then if the ADT has a destructor it schedules the destructor after the contents. In the old `destructor_call_block`, after constructing the destructor/async-drop block, the elaborator created a new block, inserted `clear_drop_flag(block_start, self.path, DropFlagMode::Shallow)` at its start, and returned `drop_flag_test_block(destructor_block, succ, unwind)` so that only the destructor call itself was guarded by the local drop flag. For `Box`, `open_drop_for_box_contents` routes the `Box` destructor through this function, and the allocator field drop is emitted after that destructor while still guarded by the same local drop flag.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was to clear the top-level local drop flag shallowly at the start of the destructor block and to guard only the destructor call with a drop-flag test. For a conditionally dropped `Box<T, A>` where the box destructor runs, this cleared the same flag that guards the subsequent allocator (`A`) drop, so the allocator drop was skipped. The fix removes the clear/test from `destructor_call_block` (and the async branch) and instead wraps the whole ADT destructor block (including box deallocation and allocator drop) in `self.drop_flag_test_block(destructor_block, contents_drop.0, contents_drop.1)`, leaving the flag set until the later drop-ladder code clears it. The PR describes this as: "Clearing Box's drop flag after running its destructor can cause it to skip dropping its allocator, so just don't. Its cleared by the drop ladder code afterwards already."
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR locals of ADT type that have a drop flag because they are conditionally initialized/moved, specifically `Box<T, A>` with a custom allocator `A: Drop` and contents `T: Drop`, where one control-flow path moves out/drops the box contents and another drops the whole box. Also covers non-`Box` ADTs with destructors, async-drop types, and the currently-unreachable case of a union/`ManuallyDrop` with a destructor plus a drop flag. Requires `#![feature(allocator_api)]` (and `async_drop` for the async tests); the MIR regression test is annotated `//@ needs-unwind`.
analysis.trigger: Elaborating the drop of a conditional `Box<T, A>` local where the box's destructor path is taken and a drop flag also guards dropping the allocator field: the old destructor block cleared that flag before the allocator drop, so the allocator was not dropped. A reproducer has `A: Drop`, `T: Drop`, and branches such as `if true { drop(*b); } else { drop(b); }`.
preconditions: The local is an ADT with an elaborated destructor, here a `Box<T, A>` using the allocator API.
The allocator type `A` implements `Drop`, so dropping it is semantically observable.
The box contents type `T` implements `Drop`, matching the issue note that removing `HasDrop`'s `Drop` impl made behavior correct.
The local requires a drop flag due to conditional initialization/move, e.g. contents moved out on one path and the box dropped on another.
The test uses `#![feature(allocator_api)]`; the MIR test also declares `//@ needs-unwind`.
For the async-drop variant, `#![feature(async_drop)]` is enabled and sync vs async contexts select different destructor paths.
pitfalls: Do not clear a local's drop flag inside or at the start of its destructor block: the same flag may guard later drops such as the box allocator field, causing them to be skipped.
Guard the entire ADT destructor chain (box destructor plus allocator drop) with the drop flag test rather than guarding only the destructor call.
The async-drop branch had the same clear-flag pattern and must be fixed alongside the synchronous destructor path.

The union/`ManuallyDrop` case now calls `span_bug!` when it has a destructor and a drop flag, because those are only open-dropped in `DropShimElaborator` which has no drop flags; a future `DerefMove`-like feature could make this reachable.
Borrowing restrictions and post-copy flag overwrites are separate conditions; the observed failure is specifically the flag being cleared before the allocator drop, not a borrow or copy-order issue.
The PR includes a `known-bug: #143658` async test where the async version is never called; do not treat that annotation as part of the fixed behavior.
analysis.testStrategy: Pair a run-pass semantic test with a MIR diff test. In `tests/ui/drop/box-conditional-drop-allocator.rs`, use a `DropCheckingAllocator<'a>(&'a Cell<bool>)` whose `Drop` sets the cell, construct `Box::new_in(HasDrop, DropCheckingAllocator(&dropped))` with `HasDrop: Drop`, conditionally move out with `if true { drop(*b); } else { drop(b); }`, then `assert!(dropped.get());`. Add `tests/mir-opt/box_conditional_drop_allocator.rs` with `//@ test-mir-pass: ElaborateDrops` and `//@ needs-unwind`, emitting `main.ElaborateDrops.diff`, to check that the flag is no longer cleared before the allocator drop and that the allocator drop is guarded by the still-set flag. Add async-drop run-pass tests with `//@ check-run-results` comparing printed sync-vs-async destructor output, and keep the `//@ known-bug: #143658` annotation only for the unrelated async call bug.
analysis.summary: ElaborateDrops bug fix: clearing a Box's drop flag at the start of its destructor block skipped the allocator's drop because the same flag guards the allocator field. The fix removes the early shallow clear and destructor-only flag test, and instead guards the whole ADT destructor block with one drop-flag test, leaving clearing to the later drop ladder. Adds run-pass and MIR-diff regression tests for conditional Box drops with a dropping allocator.
